title: JH&P AI-Embedded Client Onboarding
subtitle: A client application taken from first login to accounts opened, across the JH&P Portal, Onboarding and Portfolio sites

100.title: Rebecca's own front door
100.body: The JH&P Portal replaces the 44-page paper form. Rebecca sees her progress, her team (James and her client service executive) and exactly what happens next, in JH&P's own brand.
100.say: This is the client site. Branded, mobile-ready, and every word on it is configurable by the business.

101.title: Pick up where she left off
101.body: One button takes her into the application. Everything saves as she goes, so she can stop and come back at any time.

102.title: Six short sections, not 44 pages
102.body: The journey is tailored to her case: herself, Edward as joint applicant, the family company, accounts, source of wealth and documents. For the demo, the wand fills each step with Rebecca's answers.
102.say: In production most of this is pre-filled from Xplan and James's meeting notes.

103.title: Validated as she types
103.body: Email, mobile, date of birth and National Insurance number are checked in the form itself, so bad data never reaches the onboarding team.

104.title: Tax position
104.body: Nationality, tax residence and National Insurance number. A second tax residency only asks for a TIN when she says she has one.

105.title: Questions appear only when they apply
105.body: Dynamic rules show or hide questions based on her answers, so nobody answers a question that does not apply to them.

106.title: Edward, the joint applicant
106.body: Rebecca only gives Edward's name and email. He receives his own secure link and completes his identity section himself, in parallel.

107.title: Parties work in parallel
107.body: Each party on the case completes only their own part. The application continues while Edward does his.

108.title: The family company
108.body: Rebecca is a director of Ridge Holdings (UK) Ltd, so the journey adds a company section.

109.title: Checked against Companies House
109.body: The company number is checked against Companies House and the registered details come back automatically for her to confirm.

110.title: People with significant control
110.body: Directors and anyone owning more than a quarter of the shares are listed, each with their own status. Camilla Rose Vance is invited to verify her identity.

111.title: Accounts and objectives
111.body: The ISA and joint General Investment Account she discussed with James, with the objective and time horizon.

112.title: Preferences recorded
112.body: Long-term growth, ten years or more, excluding tobacco and controversial weapons: what she told James at their first meeting.

113.title: Where the money comes from
113.body: Source of wealth: the sale of 60% of Vance Interiors Ltd. The fields change with the type of wealth she picks.

150.title: A question mid-form
150.body: Rebecca is unsure what counts as source of wealth. Instead of emailing her client service executive, she opens the onboarding assistant.
150.say: This is the client-facing in-line assistance JH&P asked for in the RFI.

151.title: An Appian chat agent, scoped to this section
151.body: The assistant is an Appian AI agent. It knows which section she is on and answers only from JH&P's published guidance.

152.title: Answered, with its source
152.body: Plain English, with the guidance it came from. It cannot give advice or change her answers, and one click hands the question to a person instead.
152.say: Structured, safe, governed AI: grounded in your content, no advice, human handoff.

114.title: Source of wealth complete
114.body: The sale, its date and the approximate value of £2.1m. The form tells her which document we will ask for as evidence.

115.title: Three of four documents already on file
115.body: Passport, proof of address and the Companies House extract were collected automatically. Only one upload is needed.

116.title: The completion statement
116.body: She uploads the completion statement from the sale. The portal checks it is the right kind of document before accepting it.

117.title: Received, and on to signing
117.body: The statement is received and sent to Appian DocCenter in the background. Rebecca does not wait: she goes straight to signing.

118.title: Identity checks and signatures
118.body: Identity and address were already verified. Three agreements are ready to read and sign online, and Edward signs the joint mandate afterwards.

119.title: Sign and submit
119.body: One action signs the three agreements and submits the application. It locks, and the onboarding team is told straight away.

120.title: Signed and submitted
120.body: Every agreement shows as signed. What took weeks of paper and rekeying took one sitting, with every answer captured as structured data.

200.title: The client service executive's day
200.body: The Onboarding site opens on the live queue. Hartley-Vance has just submitted, two cases are past their service target, and everything that needs a person is listed on the right.

201.title: Ask about your cases
201.body: The case assistant is collapsed until it is needed. One click opens it.

202.title: Plain-English questions about live cases
202.body: The second AI ask from the RFI: natural-language case status. The question goes to an Appian chat agent that reads a live snapshot of the case records.
202.say: No report to build and no filter to set. It answers from the records as they are right now.

203.title: Answered from the live records
203.body: Carrington Trust and Ashmole Charitable Fund are past the 5-day target, and it lists what is still open on Hartley-Vance, with owners and due dates. It reads the data; it cannot change it.

204.title: Back to the queue
204.body: Hide the assistant and go to work on the new submission.

205.title: Review the submission
205.body: The new submission card opens the case straight on the Application tab.

206.title: Everything the client gave, in one place
206.body: Her answers, read-only and grouped as she saw them, beside the evidence she uploaded. Nothing has been rekeyed.

207.title: DocCenter is already reading
207.body: Appian DocCenter is extracting the completion statement with a trained model. The review task appears here when it finishes.

208.title: The case overview
208.body: The Overview shows what is outstanding on the case and who owns each item.

209.title: What stands between the case and approval
209.body: Each open item has an owner, a due date and a one-click action: the PEP match to review, Edward's section, the submission and the extracted statement.

210.title: Xplan, Pulse, Symphony, Azure
210.body: The four systems JH&P named, with the sync status of each, read from the integration log. Pulse and Symphony are written to on approval.

211.title: Parties
211.body: Every person and entity on the case.

212.title: Multi-party onboarding
212.body: Applicants, the company, its director and the accountants, each with their own screening and invite status, and a resend invite where needed.

213.title: Documents
213.body: All evidence and agreements for the case.

214.title: Evidence, with DocCenter status
214.body: Passport, proof of address and the Companies House extract on file; the completion statement awaiting review; the agreements signed.

300.title: A possible PEP match
300.body: Camilla Rose Vance, a director of the family company, has a weak 38% match against a regional councillor. Review match opens the screening check in place.

301.title: The screening check
301.body: What we send to the screening provider: name, year of birth, nationality, residence and her role on the case.

302.title: Run the screening check
302.body: One click calls the screening provider (mocked for the demo) and starts the JHP screening agent, an Appian process agent.

303.title: The agent reviews the match
303.body: The provider record comes back and the screening agent compares it with what JH&P holds, in the background.

304.title: Logged with a reference
304.body: The check is recorded with the provider's reference and time, for the audit trail.

305.title: Identifier by identifier
305.body: Name and year of birth match. Addresses (London against Edinburgh), directorships and public role all differ.

306.title: The agent advises
306.body: The screening agent recommends no match and explains why: two strong identifiers clearly differ and the score is low. Its reasoning is kept on the file.
306.say: The agent advises. A person decides, and both are in the audit trail.

307.title: A person decides
307.body: The client service executive records the decision: not the same person.

308.title: Reasoning for the file
308.body: Her reasoning is required and stored with the decision.

309.title: Confirm the comparison
309.body: She confirms she has compared every identifier herself, so the decision is never a rubber stamp of the AI.

310.title: Confirm the decision
310.body: The decision is validated before it is saved.

311.title: Four eyes, without the wait
311.body: The match clears now, and the Head of Compliance is emailed for second approval. Segregation of duties without stalling the case.

312.title: Second approval requested
312.body: The request to compliance is shown on the case, with the decision, reasoning and provider reference, and logged in the integration log.

313.title: Cleared
313.body: The PEP item has moved to Done. Three items remain.

400.title: DocCenter has finished
400.body: The completion statement has been read. Reconcile in DocCenter opens the review task.

401.title: Accept the task
401.body: Review is a governed task: accepting it stops two people working the same document.

402.title: Appian DocCenter: reconcile fields
402.body: 32 fields extracted from the six-page statement, each with its confidence, side by side with the document itself.

403.title: Check, correct, highlight
403.body: Any value can be corrected by highlighting it on the document. Net proceeds of £1,968,400 are what the client actually received.

404.title: Submit the review
404.body: The reviewed values are written to the case as structured data, and compared with what Rebecca declared.

405.title: A mismatch, raised by AI
405.body: Net proceeds are 6.3% below the £2.1m declared, outside the 5% tolerance set by the business, so an evidence-mismatch item is raised automatically.

406.title: Review the evidence beside the decision
406.body: The statement opens next to the decision. The gross price matches; the difference is deal fees. She accepts the evidence, or could ask the client to explain.

407.title: A note for the file
407.body: Every resolution carries a note, written to the audit trail.

408.title: Resolved
408.body: The mismatch is closed with the reason recorded.

410.title: Edward's section
410.body: Edward is travelling. The executive has confirmed with him by phone.

411.title: How it was resolved
411.body: The form fits the item: for information requests, how it was resolved.

412.title: Recorded
412.body: The note goes on the file.

413.title: Resolve
413.body: The item closes and the case moves on.

414.title: Back to the application
414.body: With the checks done, the application review can be closed.

415.title: Mark the application reviewed
415.body: Closes the review item raised when Rebecca submitted, and moves the case to Checks.

416.title: Send for approval
416.body: Guarded: the button refuses while anything blocking is still open. Now the case goes to James, with a case summary drafted by AI from the record.

417.title: With the portfolio manager
417.body: The case is with James Horniman for approval, and the summary is on the Overview.

418.title: The audit trail
418.body: Every action on the case, by the client, staff, services and AI.

419.title: Who did what, and why
419.body: Filterable by people, automated services and AI, with the detail of each entry, including the agents' reasoning.

500.title: The JH&P Portfolio site
500.body: A separate site for portfolio managers, in a different palette, on the same platform. James sees his pipeline and what is waiting for him.

501.title: Everything he needs on one screen
501.body: The AI-drafted case summary, the client with identifiers masked for his role, and the checks before approval: identity, screening, source of wealth, parties, risk rating and segregation of duties, each worked out from the case record.

502.title: Checks computed from the record
502.body: Identity, screening, source of wealth, risk rating and segregation of duties: each check is worked out from the case data, not ticked by hand.

504.title: Approve and open accounts
504.body: One approval writes back to Pulse (accounts), Symphony (portfolio) and Xplan (client status), and tells Rebecca.

505.title: Approved
505.body: The case is opened, with the write-back to each system logged.

600.title: Rebecca sees it straight away
600.body: Her portal shows the accounts open, with a message from her team. No chasing, no post.

700.title: Onboarding MI, live
700.body: Open and late cases, time to open, straight-through document rate, answers pre-filled and AI actions, computed from the case records.

701.title: Where work waits, and where AI is used
701.body: Cases by stage, what open cases are waiting on, back-office sync health, and every place AI is used and checked.

702.title: Changed by the business, with no release
702.body: Guidance, tooltips, dropdown options, required fields, service levels and risk weights are edited here and apply immediately. Journeys and integrations change in Appian Designer, through release approval.
